question.leadin: This man arrested the "Gang of Eight" which led a coup in August 1991 to remove him from power.
question.text: Name this Soviet president who was the eighth and final leader of the USSR before its downfall.
question.clue: This leader, who described his diplomacy with the "Sinatra Doctrine," appointed Eduard Shevardnadze as his Minister of Foreign Affairs and succeeded Constantin Chernenko.

swap.text: This country was the first to mobilize forces to support Serbia, although it withdrew from the war after a 1917 revolution deposed its king Nicholas II.
swap.clue: This country occupied Kokand and Khiva in the late 19th century.

question.text: Peter's reforms of Russia included decreasing the power of the boyars by establishing this system with fourteen levels of military, judicial, and civil service titles.
question.clue: Catherine the Great provided an automatic seven-year promotion clause within this system, which created a merit-based bureaucracy of civil service starting in 1722.

swap.leadin: The most famous events of this name are the brutal crackdown of a 1965 civil rights march in Alabamaand a 1972 massacre of Northern Irish civilians in Derry.
swap.text: Give this multi-word name shared by several dozen events, typically instances of violence by soldiers orpolice against protesters.
swap.clue: The first day of the Battle of Paardeberg during the Second Boer War was given this name, as was the beating of protesters by police during the Selma to Montgomery March.

question.leadin: A ruler of this polity named St. Olga set an enemy town ablaze by telling her soldiers to attach sulfur to birds and release them into the city.
question.text: Name this medieval Slavic federation occupying much of modern-day Ukraine. Prince Oleg of Novgorod was the first ruler of this state.
question.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

swap.text: During the Time of Troubles, a group of three individuals were given this collective name after they all claimed to be the youngest son of Ivan the Terrible.
swap.clue: This figures who marched from the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth into Moscow, where their Cossack supporters installed them as tsars.

question.leadin: It saw the bloodiest single day of the French invasion of Russia, and included fighting on the Raevsky redoubt.
question.text: The Grande Armee defeated Russian forces in this battle, despite their use of Bagration fleches. The victor of this battle later waited in vain for Tsar Alexander I's surrender after Moscow was occupied.
question.clue: Pierre Bezhukov spends most of this battle in a battery at the Raevsky Redoubt, and Mikhael Kutusov is described as being inactive during it.

swap.leadin: He was a sworn brother of the Khan of the Golden Horde, to whom he paid tribute.
swap.text: Name this Grand Prince of Vladimir and Novgorod, a Russian national hero who fought the Teutonic Knights.
swap.clue: This man served as an intermediary between the various Russian rulers and the Mongols under Sartaq Khan of the Golden Horde, whose support made it possible for this man to become Grand Prince of Vladimir.

question.text: The G7 became the G8 when, despite its weak economy, this country was added for political reasons. For calendar year 2006, its president occupies the chair of the G8.
question.clue: The mostly-defunct political party Yabloko is a protest voice in this country.

swap.leadin: Name these other royal houses toppled by World War I.
swap.text: This ruling family of Russia was wiped out at Yekaterinaburg during the October Revolution.
swap.clue: Anna Anderson claimed to be a lost member of this house.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Crimean War.
question.text: Most of the War's action concerned the Allies' besiegement of this heavily fortified, Russian held city on the Black Sea, which finally fell after nearly a year when French forces secured Malakhov, a strategic hill to its southeast.
question.clue: William Howard Russell coined a name for troops who fought off an attack on this city by General Liprandi.

swap.text: More substantially, Catherine founded this educational establishment, the first for women in Russia. Its building would house the Bolshevik headquarters during the October Revolution.

question.leadin: Originally sharing the monarchy with his sickly half brother, Ivan V, he modernized Russia and eventually removed his half-sister Sophia from power.
question.text: This is what Russian Tzar who fought the great Northern war against Charles XII of Sweden?
question.answer: Peter I or Peter the Great
question.clue: This ruler tortured a son named Alexei who died in jail.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about early Russian expansion into Siberia.
swap.text: The expansion was facilitated by Ivan the Terrible's conquest of this Tatar city, which he celebrated by building a cathedral in Moscow named for it. Today, this city is the capital of Tatarstan.
swap.clue: Both Dmitry Pozharsky and Mikhail Kutuzov credited military successes to praying to an icon of the Theotokos named for this city.

question.leadin: Name these groups of landed nobility.
question.text: This group formed a namesake duma whose power was severely curtailed in Peter the Great's reforms. Ivan the Terrible forced them to perform service for the Tsar in exchange for land.
question.clue: To undermine the influence of these people, a tsar introduced a system in which collegiate registrars were graded "K-14."

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Alexander Nevsky.
swap.text: Somewhat paradoxically, Nevsky was prince of this city and republic in modern Russia which remained unconquered by the Mongols and today houses the Milliennium of Russia monument.
swap.clue: This city's St. Sophia Cathedral is home to the bones of Yaroslav the Wise.

question.leadin: One aspect of Ivan the Terrible's political success was the control he exerted over his own succession. All of that ended when he beat his son to death by mistake in 1581.
question.text: Ivan was then succeeded by this younger son, under whose rule operational control was left to this man's brother-in-law Boris Gudonov.
question.clue: This son of Ivan the Terrible was the last Rurikid ruler. He was succeeded by Boris Godunov after dying without heirs.

swap.leadin: This figure retired to the New Jerusalem Monastery after opposing Tsar Alexis's 1649 law code, which allowed monastery lands to be taxed.
swap.text: Name this figure, whose introduction of rites such as signing the cross with three fingers angered Old Believers like Avvakum, leading to a schism known as the Raskol.

question.leadin: He succeeded Ivan Samoilovych as hetman.
question.text: Name this Cossack who joined with Charles XII against Peter the Great in the Great Northern War in a failed attempt to unite Ukraine.
question.clue: This badass who chose to ally with Sweden's Charles XII against Peter the Great in an effort to preserve Cossack autonomy over Ukraine.

swap.leadin: This war was touched off when troops under Jacob de la Gardie captured a fortress at Ladoga.
swap.text: Name this 1610 to 1617 war between Russia and Sweden, which ended with Sweden receiving large territorial gains in the Treaty of Stolbovo.
swap.clue: This war, launched by Gustavus Adolphus on the fledgling state of Mikhail Romanov, was justified by Russia's refusal to hand over Novgorod to the forces of Jacob de la Gardie. It forced the Treaty of Stolbovo, which cut off Russian Baltic access and stretched Swedish territory to Lake Ladoga and Lake Peipus, leading to the high point of Swedish power.
